name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>; accurately names the action (enqueue a MISS floating indicator). Sibling to fd2_show_damage_number. No Ghidra address residue. Confirmed by callers (all post-hit-fail / dodge / resist paths) and by the MISS sprite-id table @ 0x5204A it reads.
purpose: Enqueue a 4-slot 'MISS' floating text indicator over a target character's tile when an attack misses or the target dodges/resists.
logic_summary: Primes a 4-byte work buffer from data_fd2_battle_miss_indicator_sprite_ids (@0x5204A). Fetches the target runtime char and applies the same battle-view viewport cull as fd2_show_damage_number (x exclusive-lower/exclusive-upper via origin_x-1 and origin_x+max_x; y inclusive-lower/inclusive-upper via origin_y-1 and origin_y+max_y); if the target tile is outside the window it returns without touching the queue. Otherwise, for char_iter 0..3 it appends one slot each to the three parallel FX queues at base index spell_aoe_count_and_fx_queue_idx: x_offset = (char_iter==1)?8:char_iter*5+2 (5px-per-row, slot 1 nudged from 7 to 8), target_char_idx = target_idx, sprite_id = sprite_ids[char_iter]. Finally advances spell_aoe_count_and_fx_queue_idx by 4. The queue is later consumed by fd2_animate_spell_projectile_paths to draw the rising 'MISS' text.

params.name: target_idx
params.semantics: Runtime-char index whose tile the MISS indicator floats over; used to index data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr for the viewport cull and stored as the target char index in the FX queue slots.
params.reason: Accurately describes the value (runtime char index used both for culling and as the enqueued target). No address residue; matches use in body.

returns.semantics: No return value. Side effect: appends 4 entries to the floating-FX queues and advances the queue count by 4 (or does nothing if the target tile is off-window).

notes: Existing src header (lines 764-794) and inline comments are already precise, accurate, and ASCII-clean; they match the Ghidra decompilation (viewport cull = correct De Morgan negation of the positive predicate; y-offset layout, parallel-queue writes, +4 advance all confirmed). No Edit to anicombt.c needed. Ghidra plate is detailed (Traditional Chinese) and consistent with the src understanding -- left as-is. Minor non-issue: Ghidra plate cites '14 callers' (call-site count, dispatch calls twice from 0x20e38/0x20fdb) vs src '13 callers' (distinct caller functions); both counts are valid, not a contradiction. No logic issues found.
